restoration_note: This chapter is governed by the recurring rhetorical formula ϩⲁⲧⲉϩⲏ ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲉ ('beforehand, before…'), each clause naming a crisis and its pre-appointed divine remedy: the Third Ambassador for the night/day separation, the ships of light for the lift through the Zone, the Judge in the Living Air for the dominion of Sin, Christ-the-blessed for Error, the stars-and-spheres for human recompense, the releasers for the dissolution, and the Great Builder for the new Aeon. The vast majority of gaps are short editor restorations of word-edges (article, prepositional ⲍⲙ̄, perfect/conjunctive prefixes, qualitative endings, lexical fragments of ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ, ⲡⲭⲣⲓⲥⲧⲟⲥ, ⲧⲥⲁⲓⲟ, ⲃⲣⲡⲉ) constrained by visible flanks and Lycopolitan grammar — all confirmable with high confidence. The longer fills ({12} ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ, {14} 'rich' antithesis, {15} reset of the formulaic ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲙⲡⲁ-, {20} ⲕⲱⲧ ⲛⲥⲉ-) are constrained by the chapter's rigid 'beforehand…' parallelism and by surviving lexical anchors on either side, and are therefore restored with moderate-to-high confidence. No gap was left unrestorable, since every break is either short edge-restoration or sits within the chapter's tight formulaic chain.

restorations.basis: Edge-restoration: ⲙ̄ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ, completing 'the Third Ambassador' from ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲱⲁⲙⲧ̄ in the previous line. Lexicon: Third Ambassador = the awakening Call of Divine Truth set before the night/day discrimination.
Initial Ⲉ of Ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩ- 'before they…' — required by visible -ⲙⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩϯⲟⲩⲱ and by the chapter's recurring 'before they raised the light' formula.
Initial ⲍⲁ- of ⲍⲁⲑⲏ (Lyc. variant of ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ 'beforehand'), continuing the chapter-wide 'beforehand, before…' formula.
Final two characters of qualitative ⲧⲁⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲧ 'destroyed,' parallel to ⲛⲉⲧⲃⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧ 'the radiant ones' in the same clause — the Judge's discrimination of righteous from corrupt.
Initial ⲁ- of perfect ⲁⲩⲧⲛⲛⲁⲩ 'they sent forth,' required by visible -ⲩⲧⲛⲛⲁⲩ and by the agentive sequence 'they sent forth the Judge.'
Initial ⲍ of Lyc. ⲍⲙ̄ '(in)' (= Sah. ϩⲙ̄), completing the locative phrase 'in the Living Air' — the Judge's throne placed in true perception (ⲡⲁⲏⲣ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ).
Indefinite article ⲟⲩ- before ⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ ⲛ̄ⲁⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ 'a righteous Judge' (predicative ⲛⲁⲣ-ⲟⲩⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ).
Initial ⲍ of Lyc. ⲍⲏⲧϥ '(from) within him' (= Sah. ϩⲏⲧ⸗ϥ̄), continuing 'cast forth from within him.'
Conjunctive ⲛ̄- prefix on ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲡⲁⲣⲭⲟⲩ 'and that they should divide them,' continuing the purpose-string of subjunctives following ⲭⲉⲕⲁⲁⲥ.
Final -ⲧⲉ of ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲉ 'before' (carry-over from preceding line ⲉⲙⲡⲁ-), completing the 'beforehand, before Error and the scandal of doctrines were manifested' formula.
Initial ⲁ- of ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth,' completing ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'manifested forth in the cosmos.'
Middle of ⲡⲭⲣⲓⲥⲧⲟⲥ 'Christ' (ⲡⲭⲣⲓ- ends preceding line, -ⲟⲥ visible). Lexicon: Apostle/Christ as Lord's sent revealed truth set against Error.
Recurring rhetorical-structural adverb opening each beforehand-clause; -ⲍⲏ visible at gap-edge, with ⲁⲛ ⲉⲙ- following exactly as in lines 28 and the closing ϩⲁⲧⲉϩⲏ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩ- formulae.
Middle of ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩⲭⲡⲟ 'before they begot' — ⲉⲙ- and -ⲟⲩⲭⲡⲟ visible flanking; standard pre-temporal subordinator construction.

The surviving clause ⲍⲛⲕⲉⲕⲁⲩⲉ ⲭⲉ ⲍⲏⲕⲉ 'others (saying) poor' demands the antithetical 'rich' member — the rich/poor pair is the inhabited example of human discrimination on the earth, set within the wheel of recompense.

≈16-character lacuna immediately preceding visible ⲧⲉ ⲁⲭⲱⲩ ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩⲍⲱⲧⲃⲉ. The chapter's rigid formulaic chain of ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲉ ('beforehand also, before…') exactly fits, with the visible ⲧⲉ completing ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲉ; the next clause introduces 'before they killed' as another crisis met by foresight.
Restoration of ⲛϩⲱⲁⲓ-(ⲟⲛ) 'days,' confirmed by line 27 ⲛⲟⲩϩⲱⲁⲓⲟⲛ 'their days' — the stars and days of the wheel of recompense.
Final ⲩ of plural suffix-pronoun ⲛϩⲏⲧⲟⲩ 'from them' (the spheres), required by 3pl reference to the souls.
Editor's ⲙⲛ ⲡ- 'with the (entire earth)' is required by ⲕⲁϩ ⲧⲏⲣⲩ̄ following — the cosmos-with-earth as the totality dissolved before the consummation.
Standard ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ idiom ('release forth'); ⲁ- (preceding) and ⲁⲃⲁ-/-ⲗⲩ̄ (next line) flank, fixing -ⲃⲁⲗ. Lexicon entry 'release': ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ.

Restoration supplies the missing first verb of the doublet ⲕⲱⲧ … ⲧⲥⲁⲓⲟ ('build and adorn'), repeated in lines 34–35 of the same beforehand about the new Aeon. Lexicon: Great Builder = Divine Wisdom in its shaping power.
Mid-word restoration of ⲧⲥⲁⲓ̈ⲟ 'adorn' — ⲧⲥ- visible, final -ⲟ traced; the verb is repeated in line 35 ⲛⲥⲉⲧⲥⲁⲓ̈ⲟ ⲙⲡⲧⲁⲓⲱⲛ.
ⲡⲉ completes ⲃⲣⲡⲉ (Lyc. = ⲃⲣⲣⲉ 'new'), modifying ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲱⲛ 'the Aeon of the new'; ⲁ- is the perfect prefix of ⲁⲩⲧⲁϩⲙ̄ 'they summoned (the Great Builder).'
Definite article ⲡ- on ⲡⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛⲉⲕⲱⲧ 'the Great Builder' — lexicon-fixed title (ⲡⲛⲁⲃ ⲛⲉⲕⲱⲧ / ⲡⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛⲁⲣⲭⲓⲧⲉⲕⲧⲱⲛ).
